topic.title: General Time-Series Forecasting and Foundation Models
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Time-series models must capture temporal structure across different variables, sampling patterns, and application domains. This cluster includes recurrent forecasting, spectral representations, probabilistic prediction, and large pretrained models. The recent focus is on reusable representations that support new datasets or tasks without extensive retraining.
topic.whyItMatters: A model tuned to one dataset may fail when its frequency content, horizon, or uncertainty changes. General forecasting requires both shared structure and mechanisms that preserve domain-specific information rather than assuming all temporal data behave alike.
topic.evolution: The earliest representatives use recurrent models, direct multi-step prediction, and mixtures of experts. Recent work adds spectral attention and multi-domain pretraining. The 2025–2026 examples use continuous generative objectives, adaptive transfer, multiscale tokenization, and unified masking to extend beyond point forecasting toward probabilistic prediction, reconstruction, and broader time-series analysis.
openQuestions: What makes a pretraining corpus representative of unseen temporal regimes?
How can probabilistic forecasts remain calibrated when resolution or domain changes?
